notes: Positives must fire animate and land in the right mode: build writes code from the gate and the tables, or refuses at the gate; review returns a Before/After/Why table and Block or Approve; audit is read-only, severity-ranked, and stops for a pick; find caps its list and names rejected candidates. Negatives sit on the real borders: designer (visual direction), /debug (a broken animation), mobile-developer (React Native), the project's Astro route doctrine (a client router is the project's call). Run one invocation per case id with --threshold 1.0; prose assertions use (?i) regex because responses capitalise sentence-initially.

evals.prompt: Add an open/close animation to the dropdown menu in src/components/Menu.tsx. It uses Base UI.
evals.expected_output: Fires animate in build mode. Names the tier (occasional) and the purpose (spatial consistency), scales from the trigger with transform-origin, enters from scale(0.95) plus opacity 0 on the strong ease-out curve at 150-250ms, ships prefers-reduced-motion, and writes the code rather than offering options.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Names the frequency tier or the purpose from the gate.
assertions.check: regex: (?i)(occasional|spatial consistency|state indication|preventing a jarring change)

assertions.description: Scales from the trigger, not from centre.
Uses the strong ease-out curve from the table, not an approximation.
Enters from a near-full scale rather than scale(0).
Ships reduced motion with the animation.
Duration lands in the dropdown budget.

evals.prompt: Animate the command palette open and close — it is on Cmd+K and I want it to feel smooth.
evals.expected_output: Fires animate, runs the gate, and refuses: a keyboard-initiated action met 100+ times a day gets no animation. States which question killed it, cites Raycast or the frequency tier, and offers the non-motion alternative — an instant open, press feedback on the items at most. Writes no open/close animation.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Refuses on frequency or keyboard grounds, stated positively.
assertions.check: regex: (?i)(no animation|should not animate|does not animate|stays instant|instant)

assertions.description: Names the disqualifier.
Offers the non-motion alternative.
Does not write an open/close transition for the palette.

evals.expected_output: Fires animate in review mode. Returns a Before/After/Why findings table naming transition: all, ease-in and scale(0) with exact replacements from the tables, the verdict by tier, and an explicit Block.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Produces the findings table header.
Flags transition: all.
Flags ease-in and replaces it with the strong ease-out.
Flags scale(0) and replaces it with a near-full scale plus opacity.
Closes with an explicit Block.

evals.prompt: Audit the motion across our React app and give me a roadmap of the animation fixes worth doing.
evals.expected_output: Fires animate in audit mode. Runs recon (stack, tokens, personality, frequency map), sweeps the eight categories read-only, vets findings at file:line, returns one severity-ranked table ordered by leverage, and stops for the user to pick before writing plans into the plan directory.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Runs recon before judging.
Ranks by severity.
Stays read-only on source and writes plans only.
Stops for the user to pick before writing plans.
Cites findings at file:line.

evals.prompt: What could be animated in the dashboard to make it feel more alive? It feels flat.
evals.expected_output: Fires animate in find mode. Sweeps the seams, gates every candidate, returns at most 5-7 suggestions with exact values, and a rejected-candidates section naming what was deliberately not suggested and which gate question killed it — on a dashboard, a short list.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Names the rejected candidates section.
Every suggestion carries an exact value.
Names the gate question that killed a rejection.
Practises restraint on a dashboard.

evals.prompt: The landing page looks like every other SaaS page. Give it a real look and feel that is ours.
evals.expected_output: Routes to designer for the visual direction: subject, palette, type, signature. Motion is at most the mood line in the direction contract; no curve or duration is chosen here.

assertions.description: Routes to designer.
Does not choose a curve.
Does not open a motion findings table.

evals.prompt: The drawer stopped animating after we upgraded Motion — it just snaps open and the console says TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'animate').
evals.expected_output: Routes to /debug: reproduce, isolate, find the root cause of the TypeError. Review mode judges motion that runs; this does not run. No findings table, no easing advice before the error is understood.

assertions.description: Routes to the debug workflow.
Does not open a motion findings table.
Does not tune easing before the error is understood.

evals.prompt: Add a spring animation to the bottom sheet in our Expo app so it feels native.
evals.expected_output: Routes to mobile-developer with Reanimated on the UI thread. None of the CSS recipes apply; no @starting-style, no cubic-bezier tokens.

assertions.description: Routes to the mobile lane.
Does not reach for a CSS recipe.
Does not hand over CSS curve tokens.

evals.prompt: Add page transitions between routes on our Astro site so navigation feels smoother.
evals.expected_output: Reads the project's route doctrine first — and the landing-page-design Astro floor when this is a landing or marketing page. Whether a client router (ClientRouter) exists at all is the project's call. A static-MPA project gets no transition router; only after that decision would any motion be tuned.

assertions.description: Goes through the project's Astro route doctrine first.
Treats the client router as the project's decision.
Does not write a crossfade recipe before that decision.
